previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring tube feeds, multiple gastrostomy placements, and subsequent bypass reversal was admitted to the surgery service for two days of epigastric/mid-abdominal burning pain with nausea and inability to tolerate solid oral intake, with one red-tinged brown emesis on arrival. Evaluation included labs without acute abnormalities and an upper GI contrast study showing no leak, stricture, or obstruction (mild reflux noted). Nutrition was managed via G-tube with careful formula and rate adjustments after intolerance to Vivonex at higher rates; she ultimately tolerated Jevity 1.5 at goal 45 mL/hr with manageable baseline nausea after antiemetic adjustment to prochlorperazine as needed and addition of erythromycin for motility. Given her hypoglycemia history, she was monitored closely and supported with dextrose-containing IV fluids until stable on goal tube feeds with stable blood sugars and hemodynamics, then discharged home ambulatory with tube-feeding instructions, medication updates, and surgical clinic follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs. ___ was admitted on ___ after calling the office with 
c/o burning abdominal pain and being told to present to the ED. 
A KUB was obtained to rule out obstruction and was negative. She 
was started on an IV PPI, cholestyramine for her reflux and 
compazine for nausea.  Her home erythromycin was continued for 
gastroparesis. Her tube feeds were continued and she was allowed 
her baseline stage 3 diet. Her tube feeds were increased as her 
caloric intake and presenting nutritional status were poor. GI 
was consulted and recommended the addition of ranitidine to her 
regimen, which was implemented. They also recommended EGD to 
better characterize her pathology which was done on ___. It 
demonstrated clean-based ulcerations and gastric friability 
adjacent to the previous surgical anastomosis, as well as antral 
erythema consistent with gastritis. Her symptoms at this point 
were improving on antacid therapy and she was able to take 
excellent PO. Her tube feeds were decreased to her outpatient 
rate and she was restarted on her other home medications. Her 
pain was well-controlled, she was having good bowel and bladder 
function, and she was ambulating readily. With goals of care met 
she was discharged having increased her home pantoprazole dose 
from 40 mg PO daily to BID, and she was also started on 
cholestyramine 4 gm BID and Ranitidine 150 mg Daily. As she 
already had an outpatient appointment scheduled for ___ this

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital with esophageal burning. 
Therefore, you were given an IV medication to help protect your 
esophagus and stomach from acid and underwent an EGD to evaluate 
why you have such persistent acid reflux. Your EGD showed you 
have irritation of your stomach and esphagus and a narrowing of 
part of your digestive tract that makes it more likely for you 
to have reflux. Our GI team recommended you continue your 
antacid medications and try to position your body as upright as 
possible to optimize your stomach's chances of emptying. Your 
diet was advanced and you were tolerating increased oral intake 
well, so your tube feeds were decreased. You are now preparing 
for discharge to home with the following instructions:

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.

Please resume all regular home medications, unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.

Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids.

Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery while taking narcotic 
pain medications.

We wish you a speedy recovery,
Your ___ Care Team
